Leyla is a Postdoctoral Fellow in the <a href="https://icahn.mssm.edu/about/artificial-intelligence">Windreich Department for
AI & Human Health at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount
Sinai</a>. Her work lies at the intersection of neuroscience, AI, and
cognitive science, integrating approaches from geometry,
topology, and information theory to understand how systems with
different learning mechanisms (i.e.: biological and artificial
neural networks) acquire, generalize, and represent perceptual
information.

After receiving her PhD in Computational Cognitive
Neuroscience from Rutgers University’s <a href="https://sasn.rutgers.edu/rubic">Brain Imaging Center</a>,
she was also a joint-postdoc in the <a href="https://www.cmu.edu/dietrich/psychology/caoslab/">Concepts and Actions Lab</a> at
Carnegie Mellon University and in the <a href="https://proactionlab.fpce.uc.pt/">ProAction Lab</a> at the
University of Coimbra. Before that, she spent multiple years
researching how children acquire and apply causal reasoning
and inference in the <a href="https://projects.iq.harvard.edu/ccdlab/people/elizabeth-bonawitz">Computational Cognitive Development
Lab</a> and at the <a href="https://www.ceu.edu/unit/cognitivescience">Central European University's Cognitive Science
Department</a>. and received an MA in linguistics from the Utrecht
University.
